TechWalls Awards: The Best Products at IFA 2026

By Tuan Do

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:37
Instaread

IFA 2026 is shaping up to be one of the most interesting editions of the show in recent years. Beyond the usual upgrades to laptops, TVs, smart-home devices, and appliances, this year’s event is showcasing products that genuinely rethink familiar categories. At TechWalls, I wanted to highlight 5 products that stood out to me the most.

Best E-Bike: AOTOS Flux X26 Pro

AOTOS’s Flux X26 Pro doesn’t look like a typical electric bicycle. It is a future-ready smart e-bike designed specifically for real city roads. It combines an integrated aluminum frame and concealed battery with 20×4-inch fat tires, giving it a distinctive look while providing a comfortable and capable ride.

The Pro performance setup features a 1,500W rated motor with 2,000W peak power, making it suitable for everyday urban riding as well as steeper roads and more demanding conditions. AOTOS has also backed the bike with verified testing covering braking, speed, range, climbing ability, and thermal performance.

What really makes the T26 Pro stand out, though, is its smart functionality. Keyless Access lets you unlock the bike through proximity sensing, NFC, or a passcode, while the AOTOS app provides navigation, ride-data tracking, and smart vehicle management.

Best Robot Vacuum: iRobot Roomba Max 875 Combo

Robot vacuums have become incredibly capable, but I think the biggest challenge facing the category is still the same: Can a robot actually clean carpets as well as a good traditional vacuum? The iRobot Roomba Max 875 Combo takes a very interesting approach to that problem.

Its headline feature is SealForce technology. Instead of simply increasing suction power, the robot lowers a skirt from its chassis when cleaning carpets, creating a tighter seal around the carpet fibers and directing airflow where it matters. iRobot combines this with a vane-style blower capable of up to 35,000 Pa of suction.

The 875 Combo isn’t just about vacuuming, either. It includes a PowerSpin Max roller mop, heated ThermaMist technology for treating stubborn stains, and an AutoWash Dock that can wash and dry the mop while handling other maintenance tasks. LiDAR and cameras also help with navigation and obstacle avoidance.

At $1,199 in the US, it certainly isn’t inexpensive, but this is exactly the kind of innovation I want to see from a premium robot vacuum. Instead of adding another gimmicky feature, iRobot is trying to solve one of the fundamental limitations of robot vacuums: getting deep into carpet.

Best Oral-Care Gadget: Dyson CameraJet

If you told me a few years ago that one of the most interesting products at IFA would be a toothbrush, I probably wouldn’t have believed you. Yet the Dyson CameraJet has changed my mind.

Dyson has essentially combined an electric toothbrush, camera, AI system, and water flosser into one device. A 100,000-pixel macro camera sits near the brush head and analyzes 28 images per second. Its Gap Optical Targeting technology identifies spaces between teeth and triggers a small, targeted burst of mouthrinse to clean those areas.

The camera also turns the CameraJet into something of a dental endoscope. Through the MyDyson app, users can see a live view of their mouth and receive feedback about their brushing technique and coverage. Dyson says the camera doesn’t record or store images on the device or in the cloud. At $499.99, this is unquestionably a premium toothbrush. But that’s also what makes it fascinating.

Best Smartphone Concept: Tecno Bezelless Concept Smartphone

The smartphone category has become increasingly predictable. Screens get brighter, processors get faster, cameras get better, and the overall design changes very little from one generation to the next.

Tecno’s Bezelless Concept Smartphone is interesting because it attacks one of the few design elements that has remained almost unchanged: the bezel.

The concept features a 6.78-inch 1.5K OLED display with a 144Hz refresh rate, with the edges of the panel tucked underneath the phone’s metal frame. From the front, there is essentially no traditional black border surrounding the display. Underneath the futuristic screen is a MediaTek Dimensity 7400e processor, 8GB of RAM, 256GB of storage, and a 6,000mAh battery.

Of course, there is an important catch: this is a concept phone, not a product you can buy. Tecno has not announced a production timeline, and reports indicate that the company does not currently plan to release it commercially.

That doesn’t make it less deserving of an award. In fact, concept products are often some of the most interesting things at IFA because they show us where manufacturers believe technology could go next.

Best Smart Lighting: Philips Hue Liane 360

I’ve seen countless LED light strips over the years, and most of them share the same problem: you can see the individual LEDs or the light is primarily directed in one direction.

The Philips Hue Liane 360 takes a completely different approach. Instead of looking like a traditional LED strip, it is a flexible rope light that produces illumination around its entire circumference. Its OmniGlow technology is designed to create a smooth, diffused gradient without visible individual LEDs.

This makes the Liane 360 much more versatile from a design perspective. It can be wrapped around furniture, architectural features, walls, or other objects while maintaining a consistent glow. Philips Hue also demonstrated creative installations where the rope light was suspended like a curtain or shaped into decorative lighting.

It is available in North America starting at $399.99, making it significantly more expensive than conventional LED strips. The Liane 360 isn’t really trying to compete with a $30 LED strip. It is closer to architectural lighting that happens to be flexible, colorful, and connected to the Hue ecosystem.
